01 / The defining decision

A good slap buys one fewer counterattack.

The ideal timing choice is usually obvious: hit the green center. The tension comes from executing it while the needle moves, then seeing whether the damage crosses a knockout threshold.

The fighters stand across a table. A colored meter oscillates before the player attacks. Committing a touch freezes its readout and starts a slap. If the opponent survives, the opponent counters; there is no verified active block or parry input in these sequences. The next useful choice returns when the player is ready again. At zero HP, the exchange ends in a knockout rather than granting the defeated actor another turn.

The threshold loop

Timing qualityWhere the needle stops
→
Damage per hitTiming × the power ceiling
→
Counterattack exposureSurvive fewer replies

Power can reduce the number of attacks needed. Health increases the reply budget. This relationship matters more than a spectacular damage number in isolation. The multiplication is a model of the relationship, not a recovered source formula.

E01 · A checked exchange

Start from the recorded mid-match state in fig-meter: player 82 HP, opponent 65 HP. One 35-damage slap leaves the opponent at 30; an intervening counter reduces the player to 63; another 35-damage slap brings the opponent to zero. Both HP owners remain consistent. These are remaining values in an ongoing fight, not a claim about starting max HP.

The practical lesson is a discontinuity: enough extra damage can remove a whole enemy turn. An upgrade that changes three player hits into two may be more useful than several earlier increments. A larger health pool works on the other side of that same threshold. The source does not offer a meaningful reason to aim for a weaker zone deliberately; challenge comes from precision and changing opponents.

Observed: ordered stable HP states and alternating attacks. Inferred: the threshold relationship and 19 damage in the intervening counter. Unknown: the exact mapping from needle position to damage, counterattack generation and unedited real-time input latency. The official listing also describes stopping the moving meter near its center. Google Play.

02 / Progression as relief

Two stats solve two different failures.

Power improves the attack ceiling. Health raises the capacity to survive replies. Both are bought with the same coin wallet, so spending on one delays the other. The interface keeps them close to the fight rather than introducing a separate management screen.

Source A shows Power 1 with next price 50, then Power 5 with next price 250 while Health remains 1 with price 50. Source B shows Power 2 / price 100 / meter 44, then Power 4 / price 200 / meter 65. These sampled labels support rising tiers and a changed attack readout. The edited close-ups do not establish every transaction, a global formula or an exact wallet path.

A failed attempt should answer a useful question: did the player miss the high-damage zone, need one fewer enemy reply, or lack enough HP to withstand the next reply? A final low-HP screenshot alone cannot choose among those causes.

Loss creates a decision, with a source boundary.

The checked loss card grants a displayed reward and offers a film-icon extra slap. The later same-level return has a larger wallet, but the footage cuts across the selection. It does not prove whether the player chose revival, restarted, or used a particular reset policy. The adaptation therefore defines its own free retry policy explicitly in Complete game.

Adaptation hypothesis: keep the earned loss payout beside the two optional upgrades, then offer a direct retry of the same opponent. Explain the last stable outcome in plain language. Do not require an upgrade or a paid extra to recover from failure.

The local archive pilot supports the result-to-upgrade presentation through a checked Attack Hole reward and shop pair. It supplies a design candidate, not proof of improved retention; details are in the adaptation bridge.

03 / A short, different pressure

Three chances turn precision into a budget.

Bonus objects reuse the timing action but remove the enemy reply. The scarce resource becomes the number of attempts.

A melon bonus begins at 721 target HP with three blue hand tokens. Stable samples later show 494 and then 256; tokens move from two available to one. At the last hit, fragments fly and all three tokens become gray. The final numeric HP disappears. The last displayed attack readout is 236, so a residual of 20 is an arithmetic interpretation if that readout equals resolved damage—not a directly observed final HP. The next checked scene enters level 16.

This distinction matters for reconstruction: debris can accompany a hit without certifying that the target was fully destroyed. The target game needs separate damage feedback, break confirmation and an exhausted-budget result. It must continue the route after either outcome. Source bonus payout conditions and the exact reward for a failed break remain unresolved.

The object supplies novelty cheaply: the same action can tear a piñata, scatter fruit, or buckle a prop. Material and fracture behavior should differ visibly. A different mesh with the same generic burst would lose much of the appeal.

A skin unlock becomes a tiny show: the new fighter performs a “SPECIAL MEGA SLAP” against a dummy. This creates a reason to inspect a cosmetic without adding a permanent statistical bonus. The observed celebration does not establish a skin power system.

04 / The input is small; the consequence is large

Sell the contact, then restore control.

The visible sequence has an anticipation pose, an open-hand contact, a distorted or reddened face, body displacement, and a return to the next actionable state. A knockout expands displacement into a comic fall or crowd collision. The camera often emphasizes the face or impact, then the HUD becomes readable again.

The meter is the player's attention anchor. Poses and camera movement can be extravagant after commitment, but they must not conceal the next timing opportunity. Ordinary replies need a shorter, distinct recovery from knockout spectacle so the player can recognize which state they are in.

Edited videos compress and interrupt time. No animation duration, input delay, screen-shake amplitude or music BPM is recovered here. Facial redness and distortion are visual observations; their underlying implementation is unknown.

A consumable changes an exchange.

In the checked helmet interval, the player begins at 725 HP wearing an orange football helmet. The incoming hit shows a red 195 damage overlay; a later stable HUD reads 530, and the helmet is gone. This supports a consumed defensive item with positive incoming damage. It does not establish a percentage reduction because an equivalent unprotected hit is absent.

The official listing names defensive helmets and the Golden Fire Fist as power-ups. Their exact source costs, stacking rules and multipliers are not recovered. Official feature description. The target defines earned, optional one-exchange variants rather than deriving a formula from a graphic.

Sound boundary: acquired excerpts contain audio streams, but actual listening was unavailable in this authoring environment. No original timbre, music identity, mix or acoustic synchronization is claimed. The event and music brief below is a purposeful design brief for the adaptation.

05 / Escalation without a verified ending

The wardrobe remembers; the next rival keeps moving.

Wins pay coins, advance numbered opponents and move a visible progress strip toward a chest or bonus. Prices and rewards become larger in later samples. Costume milestones offer longer-term goals alongside immediate stats. An equipped look is visible again in the next fight, making progression part of the character's identity.

The recordings include a steel-cage arena, a red-roofed courtyard, terrace architecture and Moscow/dojo imagery. These are checked visual families, not a verified chronological map of every venue or a claim that all builds use the same rotation.

The wardrobe has multiple rows and printed milestone locks. The selected late look does not prove that every item is owned. Neither a precise total skin count nor an original final boss is established.

The source continues beyond the recorded late win. The adaptation can have a designed championship ending, but that ending must not be presented as recovered original content. The full target scope includes both a satisfying tournament conclusion and continuing play.

Implementation contract / complete game

Keep the slap. Rebuild the session.

Specification status: ready with named source limits. The complete target below is designed; delivery of this report does not certify a built game's balance, art, sound or performance.

Complete-game scope

Build a portrait-first, one-player timing duel game for phone browsers and bug.games. It must also work with a mouse. The full product is a 46-bout Championship across five arena families, 15 three-attempt object bonuses, a free 16-look wardrobe, optional earned boosters, a final champion celebration, and an endless Exhibition unlocked afterward. The championship length is a deliberate adaptation; the source visibly continues to levels 47 and 48.

RouteContent and developmentCompletion / persistence
1–9 · Table schoolOpen courtyard. Broad readable meter. Teach a good hit, enemy reply and Power versus Health. Opponent silhouettes and reactions already vary.No menu blocks the first meaningful slap. Loss is recoverable without payment.
10–18 · Street terraceEuropean terrace family. Narrower precision opportunity and new rival builds: durable, hard-hitting, balanced. Introduce earned helmet.Current opponent and stats saved; optional boosters never mandatory.
19–27 · Red-roof ringCourtyard/dojo family. Distinct movement profiles with clearly announced faster or sweeping needles. Introduce earned fire-fist alternative.The same timing commitment remains the only combat input.
28–36 · Steel cageCage silhouette and stronger crowd payoff. Mix health-heavy and power-heavy rivals; tune around changing hit thresholds.Free stats remain attainable from ordinary play and bounded defeat rewards.
37–46 · Championship squareOriginal plaza architecture. Final champion has two announced meter profiles across exchanges, normal visible HP and the same alternating rules. A distinctive pose and finale distinguish the climax.Win 46 → celebration, completion record, Exhibition. No extra payment, new hidden defense input or invulnerable phase.
Every third win · 3 through 4515 bonuses drawn from ten object families: piñata, melon, scooter prop, barrel, hanging bag, log, brick stack, suitcase, fish prop, unbranded television. Repeat families with distinct material/fracture variants.Three attempts; stop early on confirmed break. Budget exhaustion also advances. Pay a small base plus a break bonus; values are design space.
Wardrobe / ExhibitionDefault plus 15 original unlocks, one per bonus milestone. Demo, inspect, equip and cancel are distinct actions. Exhibition rotates all arenas, rivals and objects and records best green streak.Owned looks persist; no combat perks. Endless mode has no invented final ending. Replay starts a fresh bout with current earned stats.

Resource graph: resolved win/loss → earned coins → Power or Health → later fight thresholds; three-hit bonus → additional coins and milestone cosmetic → inspect/demo/equip → persistent appearance; route milestones → earned booster inventory → optional one-exchange change → consumed quantity. One soft currency is sufficient. No energy, idle income, rebirth, crafting, multiple currencies or paid core power is required.

Retry and save: a loss grants a capped participation reward once per completed attempt; display it with optional upgrades and retry the same opponent at full HP. A settled result commits reward and route atomically. Save coins, tiers, route, owned/equipped looks, booster quantities, bonus-completion flags and Exhibition records. Reload during a fight restarts that opponent from its stored pre-bout checkpoint without a second reward. Reload after a result must not pay twice. Device language/music/effects settings are separate from account progression. Failed save reads are errors, not an empty new account.

Free economy condition: neither normal progress nor the final champion may require advertising or Extras. Defeat payouts must help a stuck player recover without rewarding deliberate instant failure more efficiently than completing fights. Test both offense-heavy and defense-heavy paths through the whole Championship using ordinary play; debug-unlocked late states do not validate that balance.

Five core statements

  1. C1 · Precision has a visible consequence. Freeze needle → show timing quality → resolve damage → update stable HP → either KO or enemy reply. A lethal hit suppresses the defeated actor's pending turn.
  2. C2 · Stats alter the same exchange. Power changes hits needed; Health changes replies survived. Coins are scarce enough to make the next upgrade intelligible, but free retries always remain available.
  3. C3 · Bonus pressure is an attempt budget. Reuse the touch, remove the counterattack, spend one of three tokens per accepted hit, and distinguish damage fragments from a confirmed break.
  4. C4 · Boosters modify one exchange. Timing still matters. A helmet reduces the next incoming hit by a designed amount and is consumed; fire fist increases the next player hit by a designed amount, not an automatic win.
  5. C5 · Comedy never obscures ownership or readiness. Clear player/opponent HP, contact, consequence and recovery. An ornate celebration cannot eat the next valid input or hide the next meter.

Design space that must be tuned, not guessed as history

Choose and document the damage curve, enemy counter values, tier effects and prices, reward schedule, defeat cap, bonus HP, booster strengths, meter speeds/zone widths and motion durations as target parameters. Tune around discrete hits-to-win and replies-to-survive, not merely increasing displayed numbers. Target an initial bout of roughly 25–45 seconds as a design goal, with the first meaningful touch within 10 seconds; edited source footage cannot validate those durations. The whole game scope and C1–C5 are constraints; these numeric choices may change transparently during playtesting.

Mobile controls and settings

Use a portrait composition with two persistent HP owners at the top, meter near the fighters, and an unobstructed bottom action pad. Keep essential text readable at 390×844 without zoom. A deliberate primary-pointer down inside the ready action pad commits one hit; a hold or drag does not repeatedly attack. Release/cancel clears pressed visuals; it cannot undo an already committed hit. Ignore extra fingers and every combat tap during anticipation, impact, enemy turn or results. Do not queue taps for the next ready state.

Settings, upgrade, wardrobe and preview controls stop propagation into combat. Rotation and hidden-tab transitions pause and reflow; clear held input and freeze the needle/state rather than resolving an unseen counter. Resume from a fresh time baseline. The player can inspect before a fight, cancel a preview, and choose whether to equip. Support touch first; no hover, keyboard shortcut or swiping skill is required.

Numerals remain correctly formatted; Russian text has room to expand.Apply while paused without restarting the bout or overwriting the save. Use complete dictionaries, not machine-translated strings at runtime.

Art, animation and sound direction

Visual identity: bright low-poly toy-like fighters, oversized open hands, strong costume silhouettes and a small vivid blue table. Warm ground and architecture contrast with cool HUD colors. Keep the moving green center distinct from ornamental lighting. Use five coherent venue families, not a flat recolor for every region. Keep the body readable when the camera moves close to a face.

Asset coverage: a full shared fighter rig or an equally expressive authored 2.5D system with ready, wind-up, contact, hit-react, recover, knockout, victory and cosmetic-showcase poses; distinct rival silhouettes; all 16 costume looks; 10 object families with intact/damaged/broken states and material-specific debris; five venue sets; crowd reactions; readable meter, HP, tokens, coins and result UI. A line/circle placeholder or one generic explosion does not satisfy the intended game. Reuse rigs and textures intelligently; preserve pose quality.

Motion direction: anticipation points attention at the striker, contact produces a brief readable face/body consequence, recovery restores the HUD and next action. Nonlethal contact stays distinct from KO; debris confirms material, while the result confirms break status. Camera shake, freeze, flashes and motion lengths are tunable target choices requiring real play comparison. No exact source timing is asserted.

bug.games integration and analytics

The checked platform SDK documentation uses /sdk/bloomplay.js inside the separate-origin game iframe. The future portable HTML must run its entire core offline. Check window.parent === window before a platform import; then confirm bloomplay.isEmbedded, initialize with {preload:["save"]} and handle a rejected handshake as a service error. Standalone mode is an explicit state; it is not a diagnosis for every failed API call. SDK documentation was retrieved for this report on 05 Oct 2026.

Call loaded() once when the game is usable. Use gameplayStart()/gameplayStop() on actual play/menu/pause transitions, not each frame; if initialization finishes during play, reconcile the current active state. Make pause/resume idempotent for platform hidden/sign-in/purchase/dialog/page reasons, clear input on pause and reset the animation clock on resume. Apply onMute as the global gate over the independently saved channel gains.

For connected progress, use bloomplay.save({key:"save",cache:"slap.save.v1"}), wait for save.ready, update via save.set and flush at stable checkpoints. A failed read must not overwrite an account with defaults. Resolve a cloud/local conflict as a whole valid progression snapshot; do not merge max coins with max purchases and duplicate spending. Device settings remain separate.

Call progress.moment(name) once when its committed condition first becomes true, preserve flags across reload, and keep the declared list synchronized with actual behavior.

Optional Extras · cosmetic only, when built

A future ringside-style-pack may add distinct original outfits and a celebration beyond the free wardrobe. Show it naturally from Wardrobe after the first understood loop, with a cancelable preview; do not add a modal pitch before the first slap. Ownership never alters damage, HP, timing zones, retries or Championship access. The initial build can ship without any products or shop.

Only list an Extra in game.json once its value and states are fully implemented. Obtain sellable entries from monetization.getProducts(), show returned pricing and use purchase(id); check getEntitlements() before applying access. Confirmed ownership wins over an empty shop response, and a failed check does not revoke cached confirmed ownership. Distinguish offline, empty catalog, request failure, cancellation, pending purchase and success. Preview must revert on cancel without changing equipment or ownership. No ad API, coin top-up model or publisher payout is assumed from the checked docs.

Metadata draft: title and hook about precision slap comedy; genre casual/action, moods playful and triumphant; players:"1", coop:false, inputs:["touch","mouse"]; controls identify Tap → stop meter and commit slap. Use at most five relevant tags, a measured playtime estimate after testing, accent matching the game, seven moment names and initially products:[]. Publishing and price selection are later actions; this report does not publish a game.

Acceptance cases before implementation

CaseExpected behavior / proof
E01 equivalentThrough actual inputs, show fixed HP ownership, first damage, one living opponent reply, second lethal hit and no posthumous counter. A target parameter fixture may mirror 82/65 → 82/30 → 63/0, but ordinary balance need not copy those source values.
Precision / thresholdsAt one Power tier, green does more damage than an edge hit. At a designed tier boundary, improved damage removes an entire reply; Health instead extends survivability. Explain both outcomes visibly.
Rapid touch / cancellationTwo fingers, holds and taps during animation create at most one accepted ready hit, no queued future slap. Menus, scroll and preview controls never trigger combat. A canceled noncombat preview preserves saved equipment.
Upgrade affordability / restoreInsufficient coins show a clear refusal and mutate nothing; an affordable purchase changes wallet and exactly one tier atomically. Reload cannot duplicate either spending or effect.
Defeat → retryOne capped payout, understandable stable loss state, optional upgrade, same-opponent retry at full HP. No ad/Extra required. Compare normal recovery versus deliberate failure farming.
Three-attempt bonusExactly three accepted hits at most; confirmed early break stops remaining input. Incomplete break with fragments has an exhaustion result; route advances and rewards once in both branches.
Boosters / quantitiesChoose/cancel without consuming; consume helmet on first relevant reply and fist on first player hit. Demonstrate positive reduced helmet damage, timed fist quality, no stacking, no auto-win and untriggered item retention.
Unlock → demo → equipEvery one of 15 milestones grants the intended free look once. Preview/demo does not grant stats or alter saved selection; Equip persists an owned look; locked entries cannot equip.
Whole game by ordinary playComplete five families, all 46 bouts, 15 bonuses, free wardrobe, final celebration and Exhibition. Test offense/defense alternatives, earnings/spending and save/continue. Separately label debug late-state checks.
Late-state regressionAfter completion and repeated Exhibition/reloads, opponent, needle, HP and legal turn always exist. Test failed/old save migration and corrupted data without overwriting valid account progress.
Phone / first 20 minutes390×844 and at least one real target phone: readable Russian text, unobstructed actors/meter, one-handed touch, checkpoints in #roblox-hooks, silent-play comprehension. Record boot bytes/time, memory and frame/input behavior; desktop emulation alone does not certify phone performance.
EN/RU / audio / focusSwitch all UI in mid-bout pause without reset. Music 0 with SFX active; SFX 0 with music active; both 0; platform mute/unmute restores each gain. Background/rotation pauses without unseen results or a resumed queued tap.
Art / sound comparisonInspect anticipation/contact/consequence/recovery, KO versus nonlethal and material-specific object break. Actually listen to final licensed music and SFX. Source sound fidelity remains unverified; purposeful target mix still needs audible QA.
Platform / offlineFull standalone tour works without SDK. Connected load/start/stop, pause/mute and save errors behave correctly. Emit one result and one milestone under retry/reload. Test future Extra states separately if products are implemented.

Readiness: the complete-game specification is ready with limits on source formulas, total source catalog, revive/reset behavior, bonus payout, original audio and exact motion timing. Those limits are assigned design space above. No playable implementation, real-phone playthrough, final asset-license inventory or live bug.games purchase/publish test has occurred.

Short prompt for the future build

Build the complete mobile-first slap-comedy game specified in this HTML for bug.games, delivered as one portable HTML that also works offline. The player stops a moving needle with one thumb tap to change how many enemy replies must be survived; preserve the E01 exchange logic and C1–C5. Carry that choice through the whole Championship, three-hit object bonuses, earned Health/Power, optional one-exchange boosters, original wardrobe showcases, final champion and endless Exhibition in #complete-game. Follow #build-rules and #bridge, tune only their stated design space, and make the first 20 minutes from #roblox-hooks work through ordinary touch play. Use the exaggerated hands, readable poses, material breakage and purposeful music/SFX direction in #art-direction; implement complete EN/RU and independently persisted music/effects controls. Follow #bug-games and pass #acceptance for the whole product. This is the complete game, not an opening demo.

Parse the entire HTML including collapsed sections; strip image payload strings from textual context. Extract embedded required figures by their IDs from #evidence and inspect the extracted images with an image tool. Explain E01 from stable states before implementing. Do not treat captions, hashes or extraction counts as proof of visual understanding. All essential rules, scope, provenance and images are in this document; the builder needs no Working Notes attachment.
